briefing.headline: OpenAI and Google DeepMind race toward multi-agent AGI benchmarks

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI frontier intensified this week with major model releases and compute expansions across US and Chinese labs. Funding surged past $11B amid regulatory scrutiny and safety concerns. Prompt injection vulnerabilities continue to dominate enterprise deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4-preview with advanced agentic capabilities while Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus. DeepSeek R2 matched GPT-4o performance at lower cost. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 weights for research use.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target multi-agent risks while xAI reported internal red-teaming breakthroughs.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA shipped 1.2M Blackwell GPUs this quarter as Microsoft and Google announced $40B data center expansions. TSMC ramped 2nm production dedicated to AI accelerators.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will Chinese labs close the frontier gap by end of 2027 or will US export controls maintain a 12-month lead?
